title: The sprint start step commits the sprint's item files, so the first claim push is not refused for a dirty tree
goal: the kb-sprint skill text of the start step names `backlog.py start SP --commit`, and start --commit also commits the item files that moved from draft to todo, so `begin` and `kbgit.py sync --push` find a clean tree

run: import sys,re;t=open(".claude/skills/kb-sprint/SKILL.md").read();s=t.split("## start SP")[1].split("## run")[0];sys.exit(0 if "start SP --commit" in s else 1)

notes: Retrospective finding of the 2026-10-26 run of SP-mk6ikval: start SP without --commit left 13 item files modified and kbgit.py sync --push refused the claim push (unstaged item files); the run worked around it with set --add-notes --commit. The check reads the skill text only; the planner should add a planted run of start --commit on a fixture.
